Summarise an Aeme object

Source: R/AemeSummary.R
summarise_aeme.Rd

Reduces an Aeme with model output to an AemeSummary: daily surface and bottom values for every depth-resolved variable (the split is at the epilimnion depth, HYD_epidep, else the thermocline depth, HYD_thmcln, else half the water column), daily values for the rest, and, optionally, the observations, daily forcing and the hypsograph. The result is small enough to store and use in a dashboard, and has no model configuration, so it cannot be used to build or run a model.

Usage

summarise_aeme(
  aeme,
  model,
  ens_n = NULL,
  stats = c("mean", "min", "max", "q05", "q95"),
  keep_members = FALSE,
  vars = NULL,
  observations = TRUE,
  forcing = c("meteo", "inflows", "outflows", "water_balance"),
  profiles = FALSE,
  digits = 4L
)

Arguments

aeme

Aeme object.

model

character; models to summarise. Default: those with output.

ens_n

integer; ensemble members to use. Default NULL: all.

stats

character; statistics across members when there is more than one: "mean", "min", "max", "sd", or quantiles such as "q05" and "q95". Ignored for a single member (the stat is then "value").

keep_members

logical; also keep each member's series (as stats named "ens_001", ...). Default FALSE.

vars

character; AEME variables to keep. Default NULL: every standard variable in the output.

observations

logical; keep the observations. Default TRUE.

forcing

character; which forcing tables to keep, from "meteo", "inflows", "outflows" and "water_balance" (all by default). Use character(0) for none. They are daily means.

profiles

logical; also calculate seasonal mean profiles of temperature and oxygen (see calc_seasonal_profiles-style output in the profiles slot). Default FALSE.

digits

integer; values are rounded to this many decimal places.

Value

An AemeSummary object.

Details

With more than one ensemble member the member values are combined into the statistics named in stats.

See also

write_aeme_summary(), read_aeme_summary()
